findings.problem: The entries of `centralScalar z` already have a split simp-oriented interface in `Definitions/Def_NumberField_AdelicVolume.lean`: `centralScalar_val`, `centralScalar_apply_eq` (diagonal entries) and `centralScalar_apply_ne` (off-diagonal entries). This file adds a third, overlapping statement in `if i = j` form and untagged. The only uses are two ad hoc `simp [centralScalar_apply]` calls (lines 124 and 133). So the entry simp set is split across two competing formulations, and none of them is registered as simp. Every caller must remember to pass one by hand.
findings.proposed_change: Drop `centralScalar_apply` and `centralScalar_coe`. In the Definitions file, mark `centralScalar_apply_eq` and `centralScalar_apply_ne` as @[simp] (or add a single @[simp] entry lemma there). Then change lines 124 and 133 to plain `simp`, or to `simp [glArch_apply]`. The `ite` form can still be derived locally if wanted. The canonical normal form is `M i i = (z : 𝔸)` and `M i j = 0` for `i ≠ j`, which needs no `Decidable (i = j)` rewriting.
findings.benefit: There is one canonical way to simplify entries of a central scalar matrix. Downstream files that re-prove similar facts (the `centralScalar_coe` variants in other P2M files) can reuse it. Proofs like `archHeight_centralScalar_mul` and `centralScalar_mul_mem_siegel` no longer need hand-supplied simp arguments.

findings.excerpt: theorem ideleNorm_inv (t : (AdeleRing (𝓞 F) F)ˣ) : ideleNorm F t⁻¹ = (ideleNorm F t)⁻¹ := by
findings.problem: `ideleNorm F t⁻¹ = (ideleNorm F t)⁻¹` is a basic normal-form lemma for `TateGlobal.ideleNorm`, next to `ideleNorm_mul` and `ideleNorm_one`. It is re-proved locally here, untagged, in a `B1Assembly` namespace. The same statement is re-proved in at least two other P2M files (`G4CDIL.ideleNorm_inv` and another `ideleNorm_inv`). Because `ideleNorm_inv` and `ideleNorm_mul` are not simp lemmas, `ideleNorm_det_gone` (line 181) has to be a hand-ordered `rw` chain: `ideleNorm_mul, ideleNorm_mul, ideleNorm_inv, ← mul_inv, ...`. It also needs the reverse rewrite `← mul_inv`, which is fragile.
findings.proposed_change: Move `ideleNorm_inv` into the `NumberField.TateGlobal` namespace next to `ideleNorm_mul` in `Definitions/Def_NumberField_TateGlobalZeta.lean`, and tag it @[simp]. Its LHS has the strictly smaller form `ideleNorm F t⁻¹` and its RHS is a smaller or equal expression, so it cannot cycle. Optionally tag `ideleNorm_mul` too, so that `ideleNorm F (det (gone g))` normalizes to a product of inverses and `ideleNorm_zed_mul_self` can finish it. Delete the local and duplicated copies.
findings.benefit: Computations with idele norms of inverses and products normalize with `simp` instead of fragile `rw` chains. The three duplicate lemma statements disappear.
